records.source: וַיִּסַּ֤ע יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּאֵ֣רָה שָּׁ֑בַע וַיִּזְבַּ֣ח זְבָחִ֔ים לֵאלֹהֵ֖י אָבִ֥יו יִצְחָֽק׃
records.gloss: And set out Israel and all that [belonged] to him, and he came to Beersheba, and he sacrificed sacrifices to [the] God of his father Isaac.
pieces: So Israel set out, taking everything he owned. At Beersheba he stopped and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.

L.1: And Israel set out with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.

R.1: So Israel left with everything he had. He came to Beersheba, and there he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.

decisions.choice: Beersheba: a place where his fathers had worshiped
decisions.reason: Beersheba lay at the southern edge of Canaan, on the way to Egypt. Abraham had called on the name of the LORD there (21:33), and God had appeared to Isaac there, where Isaac built an altar (26:23-25). Jacob stops to worship before he leaves the land.

decisions.choice: the God of his father Isaac
decisions.reason: Jacob worships the God who made promises to Isaac. In the next verse God answers him with the same title: "the God of your father" (verse 3).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּמַרְאֹ֣ת הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֣ב׀יַעֲקֹ֑ב וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And said God to Israel in visions of the night, and he said, Jacob, Jacob; and he said, here I [am].
pieces: In the night God spoke to Israel in visions. "Jacob, Jacob," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called, and Jacob said, "Here I am."

L.2: And God spoke to Israel in visions of the night and said, "Jacob, Jacob." And he said, "Here I am."

R.2: That night God spoke to Israel in a vision. God said, "Jacob, Jacob!" Jacob answered, "Yes, I am here."

decisions.choice: Jacob, Jacob ... here I am: a call and a ready answer
decisions.reason: Calling the name twice marks an urgent, personal call, as with "Abraham, Abraham" (22:11). "Here I am" (hinneni) is the answer of someone ready to listen and obey (22:1; 31:11).

decisions.choice: visions of the night: a vision at night
decisions.reason: The plural "visions" can describe a single experience; God speaks to Jacob at night, as at Bethel when he first left home (28:12-15).

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָנֹכִ֥י הָאֵ֖ל אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֑יךָ אַל־תִּירָא֙ מֵרְדָ֣ה מִצְרַ֔יְמָה כִּֽי־לְג֥וֹי גָּד֖וֹל אֲשִֽׂימְךָ֥ שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And he said, I [am] the God, [the] God of your father; do not be afraid of going down to Egypt, for into a great nation I will make you there.
pieces: He said, "I am God, your father's God. Do not fear the journey down to Egypt, for it is there that I will make you a great nation.

L.3: And he said, "I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.

R.3: God said, "I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid of going to Egypt. Egypt is where I will make your family grow into a great nation.

decisions.choice: the God: El, God himself
decisions.reason: Ha-El, "the God", uses the short word El, found in titles such as El Shaddai (17:1; 35:11). God names himself as the one God of Jacob's fathers.

decisions.choice: do not be afraid to go down to Egypt
decisions.reason: Going down to Egypt was not a light step. God had told Isaac not to go there (26:2), and Abraham's stay there had gone badly (12:10-20). But God had also told Abraham that his descendants would live in a land not their own and come out again (15:13-14).

decisions.choice: a great nation: the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: God repeats his first promise to Abraham, "I will make you a great nation" (12:2). It will be fulfilled in Egypt itself, where the family grows into a people (Exodus 1:7).

decisions.choice: make your family grow into a great nation
alternatives: make you into a great nation
decisions.reason: Readable says "your family" because the nation will come from Jacob's descendants, not from Jacob alone.

records.source: אָנֹכִ֗י אֵרֵ֤ד עִמְּךָ֙ מִצְרַ֔יְמָה וְאָנֹכִ֖י אַֽעַלְךָ֣ גַם־עָלֹ֑ה וְיוֹסֵ֕ף יָשִׁ֥ית יָד֖וֹ עַל־עֵינֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will bring you up, also bringing up; and Joseph will put his hand over your eyes.
pieces: I myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I myself will bring you up again without fail. Joseph will be the one to close your eyes."

L.4: I myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I myself will also surely bring you up again; and Joseph will put his hand on your eyes."

R.4: I will go with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring your family out again. When you die, it is Joseph who will close your eyes."

decisions.choice: I myself ... surely: emphatic promise
decisions.reason: God says "I" twice with the separate pronoun anokhi, and doubles the verb "bring up". The emphasis makes the promise personal and certain.

decisions.choice: bring you up: Jacob's burial and his descendants' return
decisions.reason: The promise is kept twice over: Jacob's body is carried back to Canaan for burial (50:13), and his descendants come up out of Egypt in the exodus (Exodus 3:8).

decisions.choice: put his hand on your eyes: close your eyes at death
decisions.reason: Closing the eyes of the dead was done by the nearest family. God promises Jacob that his lost son will be with him when he dies (50:1).

decisions.choice: bring your family back out
decisions.reason: The "you" is Jacob and the people who come from him; Readable names the family because Jacob himself returns only for burial.

decisions.choice: when you die, it is Joseph who will close your eyes
alternatives: Joseph will put his hand on your eyes
decisions.reason: Readable explains the custom in plain words.

records.source: וַיָּ֥קָם יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִבְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיִּשְׂא֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־יַעֲקֹ֣ב אֲבִיהֶ֗ם וְאֶת־טַפָּם֙ וְאֶת־נְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם בָּעֲגָל֕וֹת אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥ח פַּרְעֹ֖ה לָשֵׂ֥את אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And arose Jacob from Beersheba, and carried [the] sons of Israel Jacob their father and their little ones and their wives in the carts which had sent Pharaoh to carry him.
pieces: Jacob moved on from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried their father Jacob, their little ones and their wives in the carts that Pharaoh had sent for him.

L.5: Then Jacob set out from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father and their little ones and their wives in the carts that Pharaoh had sent to carry him.

R.5: Then Jacob left Beersheba. His sons put him in the wagons that Pharaoh had sent to bring him. They also put their wives and children in the wagons.

decisions.choice: little ones: young children
decisions.reason: Taf means the small children of a household, those too young to make the long journey on foot.

records.source: וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶת־מִקְנֵיהֶ֗ם וְאֶת־רְכוּשָׁם֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָֽכְשׁוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ מִצְרָ֑יְמָה יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְכָל־זַרְע֥וֹ אִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they took their livestock and their possessions which they had acquired in [the] land of Canaan, and they came to Egypt, Jacob and all his offspring with him,
pieces: They also took the livestock and goods they had gained in the land of Canaan, and they came to Egypt, Jacob and all his descendants with him,

L.6: And they took their livestock and their goods, which they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and came to Egypt, Jacob and all his offspring with him,

R.6: They took their animals and everything they had gotten in Canaan. Jacob went to Egypt, and all his descendants went with him.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: Zera, "seed", means offspring. As in earlier chapters, Literal says "offspring" and Balanced and Readable say "descendants".

records.source: בָּנָ֞יו וּבְנֵ֤י בָנָיו֙ אִתּ֔וֹ בְּנֹתָ֛יו וּבְנ֥וֹת בָּנָ֖יו וְכָל־זַרְע֑וֹ הֵבִ֥יא אִתּ֖וֹ מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃ס
records.gloss: his sons and [the] sons of his sons with him, his daughters and [the] daughters of his sons, and all his offspring he brought with him to Egypt.
pieces: his sons and grandsons, his daughters and granddaughters. He brought all his descendants with him to Egypt.

L.7: his sons and his sons' sons with him, his daughters and his sons' daughters; all his offspring he brought with him to Egypt.

R.7: He brought his sons and grandsons and his daughters and granddaughters with him. All his descendants went with him to Egypt.

decisions.choice: his daughters: the women of his family
decisions.reason: Only two daughters of the family are named in the list, Dinah (verse 15) and Serah (verse 17). "Daughters" may include the wives of his sons, as when "all his daughters" tried to comfort Jacob (37:35).

records.source: וְאֵ֨לֶּה שְׁמ֧וֹת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הַבָּאִ֥ים מִצְרַ֖יְמָה יַעֲקֹ֣ב וּבָנָ֑יו בְּכֹ֥ר יַעֲקֹ֖ב רְאוּבֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] names of [the] sons of Israel who went to Egypt, Jacob and his sons: [the] firstborn of Jacob, Reuben.
pieces: These are the names of the family of Israel who came to Egypt, Jacob and his sons. Jacob's firstborn was Reuben.

L.8: And these are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Jacob's firstborn, Reuben.

R.8: Here are the names of the people of Israel who went to Egypt: Jacob and his sons. Reuben was Jacob's oldest son.

decisions.choice: these are the names of the sons of Israel
decisions.reason: The book of Exodus opens with the same words (Exodus 1:1-5), and gives the same count of seventy. The list marks the family's move from the land of promise into Egypt, where it will become a people.

decisions.choice: the family of Israel
decisions.reason: The list includes Jacob himself, his daughter and his grandchildren, so Balanced and Readable speak of the family or people rather than "sons".

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י רְאוּבֵ֑ן חֲנ֥וֹךְ וּפַלּ֖וּא וְחֶצְר֥וֹן וְכַרְמִֽי׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Reuben: Hanoch and Pallu and Hezron and Carmi.
pieces: Reuben's sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.

L.9: And the sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.

R.9: Reuben's sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֗וֹן יְמוּאֵ֧ל וְיָמִ֛ין וְאֹ֖הַד וְיָכִ֣ין וְצֹ֑חַר וְשָׁא֖וּל בֶּן־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִֽית׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jachin and Zohar and Shaul [the] son of the Canaanite [woman].
pieces: Simeon's sons were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin and Zohar, and Shaul, whose mother was a Canaanite.

L.10: And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.

R.10: Simeon's sons were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar and Shaul. Shaul's mother was a woman from Canaan.

decisions.choice: son of a Canaanite woman
decisions.reason: Abraham and Isaac had refused Canaanite wives for their sons (24:3; 28:1), but Jacob's sons married local women, as Judah did (38:2). The list notes it for Shaul alone.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י לֵוִ֑י גֵּרְשׁ֕וֹן קְהָ֖ת וּמְרָרִֽי׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
pieces: Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

L.11: And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

R.11: Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה עֵ֧ר וְאוֹנָ֛ן וְשֵׁלָ֖ה וָפֶ֣רֶץ וָזָ֑רַח וַיָּ֨מָת עֵ֤ר וְאוֹנָן֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן וַיִּהְי֥וּ בְנֵי־פֶ֖רֶץ חֶצְר֥וֹן וְחָמֽוּל׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Judah: Er and Onan and Shelah and Perez and Zerah; and died Er and Onan in [the] land of Canaan; and were [the] sons of Perez Hezron and Hamul.
pieces: Judah's sons were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez and Zerah, though Er and Onan had died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.

L.12: And the sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez and Zerah (but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan); and the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.

R.12: Judah's sons were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez and Zerah. But Er and Onan had already died in Canaan. Perez's sons were Hezron and Hamul.

decisions.choice: Er and Onan died; the sons of Perez
decisions.reason: Er and Onan died in Canaan as told in 38:7-10, so they are named but not counted. Perez, Tamar's son, carries Judah's line on: Hezron is an ancestor of David (Ruth 4:18-22).

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י יִשָׂשכָ֑ר תּוֹלָ֥ע וּפֻוָּ֖ה וְי֥וֹב וְשִׁמְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Issachar: Tola and Puvah and Iob and Shimron.
pieces: Issachar's sons were Tola, Puvah, Iob and Shimron.

L.13: And the sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob and Shimron.

R.13: Issachar's sons were Tola, Puvah, Iob and Shimron.

decisions.choice: Iob, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has the short name Iob (Yov). The Samaritan Pentateuch reads Jashub, the name this son has in Numbers 26:24 and 1 Chronicles 7:1. The Hebrew text is followed. Puvah is also spelled Puah in 1 Chronicles 7:1.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י זְבוּלֻ֑ן סֶ֥רֶד וְאֵל֖וֹן וְיַחְלְאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Zebulun: Sered and Elon and Jahleel.
pieces: Zebulun's sons were Sered, Elon and Jahleel.

L.14: And the sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon and Jahleel.

R.14: Zebulun's sons were Sered, Elon and Jahleel.

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה׀בְּנֵ֣י לֵאָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָֽלְדָ֤ה לְיַעֲקֹב֙ בְּפַדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת דִּינָ֣ה בִתּ֑וֹ כָּל־נֶ֧פֶשׁ בָּנָ֛יו וּבְנוֹתָ֖יו שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֹֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: These [are the] sons of Leah whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, and Dinah his daughter; all [the] persons, his sons and his daughters, [were] thirty-three.
pieces: These are Leah's sons, born to Jacob in Paddan-aram, with his daughter Dinah. Counting sons and daughters, this branch of the family came to thirty-three people.

L.15: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan-aram, together with his daughter Dinah. All the persons, his sons and his daughters, [were] thirty-three.

R.15: These are the sons that Leah had with Jacob in Paddan-aram. She also had a daughter, Dinah. In all, there were thirty-three people in Leah's part of the family.

decisions.choice: thirty-three: the count includes Jacob
decisions.reason: The names listed for Leah, leaving out Er and Onan who had died, come to thirty-two with Dinah. The total of thirty-three counts Jacob himself, named at the head of the list (verse 8). With sixteen, fourteen and seven in the other groups, this gives the seventy of verse 27.

decisions.choice: this branch of the family
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the count is of Jacob's descendants through Leah, grandchildren included.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י גָ֔ד צִפְי֥וֹן וְחַגִּ֖י שׁוּנִ֣י וְאֶצְבֹּ֑ן עֵרִ֥י וַֽאֲרוֹדִ֖י וְאַרְאֵלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Gad: Ziphion and Haggi, Shuni and Ezbon, Eri and Arodi and Areli.
pieces: Gad's sons were Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi and Areli.

L.16: And the sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi and Areli.

R.16: Gad's sons were Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi and Areli.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י אָשֵׁ֗ר יִמְנָ֧ה וְיִשְׁוָ֛ה וְיִשְׁוִ֥י וּבְרִיעָ֖ה וְשֶׂ֣רַח אֲחֹתָ֑ם וּבְנֵ֣י בְרִיעָ֔ה חֶ֖בֶר וּמַלְכִּיאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Asher: Imnah and Ishvah and Ishvi and Beriah, and Serah their sister; and [the] sons of Beriah: Heber and Malkiel.
pieces: Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah, and they had a sister, Serah. Beriah's sons were Heber and Malkiel.

L.17: And the sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malkiel.

R.17: Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah. Their sister was Serah. Beriah's sons were Heber and Malkiel.

records.source: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י זִלְפָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן לָבָ֖ן לְלֵאָ֣ה בִתּ֑וֹ וַתֵּ֤לֶד אֶת־אֵ֨לֶּה֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה נָֽפֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: These [are the] sons of Zilpah whom gave Laban to Leah his daughter; and she bore these to Jacob, sixteen persons.
pieces: These were the descendants of Zilpah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Leah. She bore these to Jacob, sixteen persons in all.

L.18: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Leah; and she bore these to Jacob, sixteen persons.

R.18: These sixteen people came from Zilpah, the servant Laban had given to his daughter Leah. They were Jacob's children and grandchildren through her.

decisions.choice: the sons she bore: her descendants
decisions.reason: "Sons" and "bore" are used broadly: the sixteen include Zilpah's grandsons, a granddaughter and great-grandsons, counted as hers.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: Balanced says "descendants" because the count includes grandchildren; Literal keeps "sons".

decisions.choice: the servant
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader who Zilpah was: Laban gave her to Leah as a servant (29:24). "Servant" as the style guide has it; Literal keeps "slave woman".

records.source: בְּנֵ֤י רָחֵל֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב יוֹסֵ֖ף וּבִנְיָמִֽן׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Rachel, [the] wife of Jacob: Joseph and Benjamin.
pieces: The sons of Jacob's wife Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.

L.19: The sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin.

R.19: Jacob's wife Rachel had two sons, Joseph and Benjamin.

records.source: וַיִּוָּלֵ֣ד לְיוֹסֵף֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָֽלְדָה־לּוֹ֙ אָֽסְנַ֔ת בַּת־פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֖רַע כֹּהֵ֣ן אֹ֑ן אֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וְאֶת־אֶפְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And were born to Joseph in [the] land of Egypt, whom bore to him Asenath [the] daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, Manasseh and Ephraim.
pieces: In Egypt, Joseph had two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim. Their mother was Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.

L.20: And to Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.

R.20: Joseph's sons Manasseh and Ephraim were born in Egypt. Their mother was Asenath. She was the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of the city of On.

decisions.choice: On: the city of the sun god
decisions.reason: On, later called Heliopolis, near modern Cairo, was a center of the worship of the sun. Pharaoh gave Joseph a priest's daughter as his wife (41:45, 50-52).

decisions.choice: Manasseh and Ephraim, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: Manasseh and Ephraim, followed by five of their sons and grandsons (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The Septuagint adds here five descendants of Manasseh and Ephraim. With them its total in verse 27 is seventy-five. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: the city of On
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the city of" so that On is understood as a place.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֗ן בֶּ֤לַע וָבֶ֨כֶר֙ וְאַשְׁבֵּ֔ל גֵּרָ֥א וְנַעֲמָ֖ן אֵחִ֣י וָרֹ֑אשׁ מֻפִּ֥ים וְחֻפִּ֖ים וָאָֽרְדְּ׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Benjamin: Bela and Becher and Ashbel, Gera and Naaman, Ehi and Rosh, Muppim and Huppim and Ard.
pieces: Benjamin's sons were Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim and Ard.

L.21: And the sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim and Ard.

R.21: Benjamin's sons were Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim and Ard.

decisions.choice: the sons of Benjamin: the heads of his family
decisions.reason: Benjamin, the youngest, is given ten sons. Numbers 26:38-40 makes Naaman and Ard sons of Bela, that is, Benjamin's grandsons, and several names differ there and in 1 Chronicles 8:1-5. "Sons" may include later descendants who became heads of Benjamin's clans.

records.source: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י רָחֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלַּ֖ד לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב כָּל־נֶ֖פֶשׁ אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: These [are the] sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob; all [the] persons [were] fourteen.
pieces: These were Rachel's descendants born to Jacob, fourteen people in all.

L.22: These are the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob, fourteen persons in all.

R.22: These fourteen people were Jacob's children and grandchildren through Rachel.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: The fourteen include Joseph, Benjamin and their sons, so Balanced says "descendants".

records.source: וּבְנֵי־דָ֖ן חֻשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Dan: Hushim.
pieces: Dan's son was Hushim.

L.23: And the sons of Dan: Hushim.

decisions.choice: the sons of Dan: one name
decisions.reason: The list keeps its set form "the sons of" even where only one name follows. Numbers 26:42 calls him Shuham.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י נַפְתָּלִ֑י יַחְצְאֵ֥ל וְגוּנִ֖י וְיֵ֥צֶר וְשִׁלֵּֽם׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel and Guni and Jezer and Shillem.
pieces: Naphtali's sons were Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer and Shillem.

L.24: And the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer and Shillem.

R.24: Naphtali's sons were Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer and Shillem.

records.source: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י בִלְהָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן לָבָ֖ן לְרָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֑וֹ וַתֵּ֧לֶד אֶת־אֵ֛לֶּה לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב כָּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ שִׁבְעָֽה׃
records.gloss: These [are the] sons of Bilhah whom gave Laban to Rachel his daughter; and she bore these to Jacob, all [the] persons [were] seven.
pieces: These were the descendants of Bilhah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Rachel. She bore these to Jacob, seven persons in all.

L.25: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel, and she bore these to Jacob, seven persons in all.

R.25: These seven people came from Bilhah, the servant Laban had given to his daughter Rachel. They were Jacob's children and grandchildren through her.

decisions.choice: the servant
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader who Bilhah was: Laban gave her to Rachel as a servant (29:29). "Servant" as the style guide has it; Literal keeps "slave woman".

records.source: כָּל־הַ֠נֶּפֶשׁ הַבָּאָ֨ה לְיַעֲקֹ֤ב מִצְרַ֨יְמָה֙ יֹצְאֵ֣י יְרֵכ֔וֹ מִלְּבַ֖ד נְשֵׁ֣י בְנֵי־יַעֲקֹ֑ב כָּל־נֶ֖פֶשׁ שִׁשִּׁ֥ים וָשֵֽׁשׁ׃
records.gloss: Every person who went belonging to Jacob to Egypt, who came out of his thigh, besides [the] wives of [the] sons of Jacob, all [the] persons [were] sixty-six.
pieces: Jacob's own descendants who traveled with him to Egypt came to sixty-six, without counting his sons' wives.

L.26: All the persons belonging to Jacob who came into Egypt, who came out of his thigh, not counting the wives of Jacob's sons, were sixty-six persons in all.

R.26: Sixty-six people went to Egypt with Jacob. All of them were his own children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren. This number does not count the wives of Jacob's sons.

decisions.choice: came out of his thigh: his own descendants
decisions.reason: The thigh stands for a man's power to father children. "Those who came out of his thigh" are his blood descendants (Exodus 1:5).

decisions.choice: sixty-six: those who traveled with Jacob
decisions.reason: The seventy of verse 27, less Jacob himself and Joseph and his two sons, who were already in Egypt, leaves sixty-six who made the journey.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֥י יוֹסֵ֛ף אֲשֶׁר־יֻלַּד־ל֥וֹ בְמִצְרַ֖יִם נֶ֣פֶשׁ שְׁנָ֑יִם כָּל־הַנֶּ֧פֶשׁ לְבֵֽית־יַעֲקֹ֛ב הַבָּ֥אָה מִצְרַ֖יְמָה שִׁבְעִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt [were] two persons. All the persons of [the] house of Jacob who went to Egypt [were] seventy.
pieces: Joseph had two sons who were born to him in Egypt. So the whole household of Jacob that came to Egypt numbered seventy.

L.27: And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt were two persons. All the persons of the house of Jacob who came into Egypt were seventy.

R.27: Joseph's two sons had been born in Egypt. So in all, seventy people from Jacob's family came to Egypt.

decisions.choice: seventy: the whole family
decisions.reason: Seventy is the sum of the four groups (33 + 16 + 14 + 7). It is also a round number for a complete whole: the nations of the world in chapter 10 number about seventy. The same count is given in Exodus 1:5 and Deuteronomy 10:22, where Moses recalls that seventy went down and the LORD made them as many as the stars.

decisions.choice: seventy, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Septuagint counts nine sons of Joseph born in Egypt here and seventy-five in all, adding the descendants of Manasseh and Ephraim (see verse 20). It has seventy-five also in Exodus 1:5, as does a Hebrew scroll of Exodus found at Qumran. Stephen's speech follows this count: "seventy-five persons" (Acts 7:14). The two totals count the family in different ways. The Hebrew text is followed.

records.source: וְאֶת־יְהוּדָ֞ה שָׁלַ֤ח לְפָנָיו֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף לְהוֹרֹ֥ת לְפָנָ֖יו גֹּ֑שְׁנָה וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אַ֥רְצָה גֹּֽשֶׁן׃
records.gloss: And Judah he sent before him to Joseph to show [the way] before him to Goshen; and they came [to the] land of Goshen.
pieces: Jacob had Judah go ahead of him to Joseph, so that Joseph could show the way to Goshen. And they came into the land of Goshen.

L.28: And he sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph, to show [the way] before him to Goshen, and they came into the land of Goshen.

R.28: Jacob sent Judah ahead to Joseph to ask him the way to Goshen. Then they all came into Goshen.

decisions.choice: to show the way before him: to get directions to Goshen
alternatives: so that Joseph would meet him in Goshen
to prepare the way to Goshen
decisions.reason: Lehorot is "to point out" or "to instruct". Judah may go ahead so that Joseph can direct the family to Goshen, or to lead the way himself. The Septuagint reads "to meet him at Heroonpolis". Judah, who pledged himself for Benjamin (43:9; 44:32), now leads the family.

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jacob as the one who sent Judah.

records.source: וַיֶּאְסֹ֤ר יוֹסֵף֙ מֶרְכַּבְתּ֔וֹ וַיַּ֛עַל לִקְרַֽאת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אָבִ֖יו גֹּ֑שְׁנָה וַיֵּרָ֣א אֵלָ֗יו וַיִּפֹּל֙ עַל־צַוָּארָ֔יו וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ עַל־צַוָּארָ֖יו עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: And harnessed Joseph his chariot and went up to meet Israel his father to Goshen; and he appeared to him, and he fell on his neck and wept on his neck still.
pieces: Joseph got his chariot ready and went up to Goshen to meet his father Israel. The moment he came before his father, he flung his arms around his neck and wept, and went on weeping a long while.

L.29: And Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to meet Israel his father in Goshen. And he presented himself to him and fell on his neck and wept on his neck a long time.

R.29: Joseph got his chariot ready and went to Goshen to meet his father Israel. When Joseph saw his father, he hugged him and cried for a long time.

decisions.choice: presented himself: he let himself be seen
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used when God "appeared" to the patriarchs (12:7; 35:9). Here the son Jacob thought dead stands before him, seen with his own eyes.

decisions.choice: fell on his neck and wept: a long embrace
decisions.reason: To fall on someone's neck is to embrace him (45:14). Od, "still" or "again", here means that he went on weeping for a long time.

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף אָמ֣וּתָה הַפָּ֑עַם אַחֲרֵי֙ רְאוֹתִ֣י אֶת־פָּנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֥י עוֹדְךָ֖ חָֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Israel to Joseph, let me die this time, after my seeing your face, that still you [are] alive.
pieces: Israel said to Joseph, "Now let death come. I have looked on your face, and I know you are alive."

L.30: And Israel said to Joseph, "Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive."

R.30: Israel said to Joseph, "Now I can die in peace. I have seen you with my own eyes, and I know you are still alive."

decisions.choice: let me die this time: I am content to die
decisions.reason: Jacob does not wish to die; he means he has nothing more to wait for. Years before he said he would go down to Sheol mourning for Joseph (37:35; 42:38). Now he can face death in peace. He lives seventeen more years (47:28).

decisions.choice: in peace
decisions.reason: Readable adds "in peace" to make clear that Jacob speaks of contentment, not a wish to die.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹסֵ֤ף אֶל־אֶחָיו֙ וְאֶל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו אֶעֱלֶ֖ה וְאַגִּ֣ידָה לְפַרְעֹ֑ה וְאֹֽמְרָ֣ה אֵלָ֔יו אַחַ֧י וּבֵית־אָבִ֛י אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־כְּנַ֖עַן בָּ֥אוּ אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Joseph to his brothers and to [the] household of his father, I will go up and I will tell Pharaoh and I will say to him, my brothers and [the] household of my father who [were] in [the] land of Canaan have come to me.
pieces: Joseph said to his brothers and to the rest of his father's family, "I am going up to Pharaoh to give him the news. I will tell him, 'My brothers and my father's family, who were living in Canaan, have arrived to join me.

L.31: And Joseph said to his brothers and to his father's household, "I will go up and tell Pharaoh, and I will say to him, 'My brothers and my father's household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.

R.31: Then Joseph spoke to his brothers and the rest of the family. "I will go to Pharaoh and let him know you are here. I will tell him, 'My brothers and my father's family have come here from Canaan to be with me.

records.source: וְהָאֲנָשִׁים֙ רֹ֣עֵי צֹ֔אן כִּֽי־אַנְשֵׁ֥י מִקְנֶ֖ה הָי֑וּ וְצֹאנָ֧ם וּבְקָרָ֛ם וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם הֵבִֽיאוּ׃
records.gloss: And the men [are] shepherds of flock, for men of livestock they have been; and their flocks and their herds and all that [is] to them they have brought.
pieces: These men are shepherds, people who have kept livestock all along, and they have come with their sheep and goats, their cattle and all their belongings.'

L.32: And the men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks and their herds and all that they have.'

R.32: These men take care of sheep and goats. They have always raised animals. They have brought their flocks and herds and everything they own with them.'

decisions.choice: sheep and goats
decisions.reason: Tson means a flock of small animals, sheep and goats together.

records.source: וְהָיָ֕ה כִּֽי־יִקְרָ֥א לָכֶ֖ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְאָמַ֖ר מַה־מַּעֲשֵׂיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And it will be when summons you Pharaoh and says, what [are] your occupations?
pieces: When Pharaoh summons you and asks what you do for a living,

L.33: And when Pharaoh calls you and says, 'What is your occupation?'

R.33: Pharaoh will call you in and ask, 'What work do you do?'

records.source: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֗ם אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִקְנֶ֜ה הָי֤וּ עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ מִנְּעוּרֵ֣ינוּ וְעַד־עַ֔תָּה גַּם־אֲנַ֖חְנוּ גַּם־אֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ בַּעֲב֗וּר תֵּשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֔שֶׁן כִּֽי־תוֹעֲבַ֥ת מִצְרַ֖יִם כָּל־רֹ֥עֵה צֹֽאן׃
records.gloss: and you will say, Men of livestock have been your servants from our youth and until now, both we and our fathers, so that you may dwell in [the] land of Goshen; for an abomination of Egypt [is] every shepherd of flock.
pieces: answer, 'We your servants have kept livestock since we were young, and so did our fathers before us.' That way you will be able to live in the land of Goshen, because Egyptians loathe everyone who herds sheep."

L.34: you shall say, 'Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth until now, both we and our fathers,' so that you may live in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians."

R.34: Tell him, 'Since we were boys we have looked after animals, and our fathers did too.' That way you will be allowed to live in Goshen. Egyptians hate shepherds and want to keep away from them."

decisions.choice: keepers of livestock: an honest but careful description
decisions.reason: Joseph himself will tell Pharaoh they are shepherds (verse 32), but he has his brothers describe themselves as men who have always kept livestock, a settled, respectable trade. The aim is that Pharaoh will place them in Goshen, apart from the Egyptians.

decisions.choice: abomination: something detestable
decisions.reason: To'evah is what a people finds offensive and will not touch. Egyptians would not eat with Hebrews for the same reason (43:32). The text gives no reason for their dislike of shepherds; its effect is that Jacob's family lives apart in Goshen and keeps its own identity.

decisions.choice: and want to keep away from them
decisions.reason: Readable spells out why the family's work leads to their being settled in Goshen, apart from the Egyptians.
